Discussion update · Architecture first

Two uses. Different tests of success.

Selected experiment

Architectural exploration

Follow a question across the repo: what runs, what code composes it, what contract it uses, why that choice was made, and what evidence supports it.

Success: useful navigation, accurate relationships, visible gaps, and an export that stays aligned as the repo changes.

Separate future use case

Teaching and explanation

A lesson chooses its audience, prior knowledge, sequence, worked examples and recall. An open graph gives a learner many possible routes; some may distract or presuppose concepts they have not learned.

Success: demonstrated understanding and transfer. A curated route through the architectural model might help, but that needs evaluation.

An Nx project is not automatically a C4 container. Containers are runtime applications or data stores; components describe functionality inside them. One source library may serve several runtime applications. Keep a mapping such as runtime app → implemented by → source project. C4 containers, components.

A concrete route: Evidence client runtime → syncs with → Evidence server runtime → implemented by → evidence-server project → declares dependency on → sync-server project. From there, inspect the source and the relevant decisions. These are different kinds of connection, even if K-Plex places several of them on the same side.

Runtime route grounded in P11 client composition, server composition and declared dependencies. The trial labels this as the inspected P11 lab view, not a complete production deployment model.

One extracted model can support several vaults.

1. Canonical repo sources

Definitions, source structure, composition declarations, ADRs and evidence keep their existing ownership.

2. A directed export model

Stable identities, types, exact relationship names, source locations and revision. Viewer-specific spatial roles are a projection of this model.

3. Vault/viewer presets

An architecture vault first; later, a documentation explorer or another viewer. Each preset selects scope, ontology mapping and presentation.

A full-repo architectural browser means every relevant area is discoverable and missing mappings are visible. It does not mean showing every file at once. Start with one vault and prove the export model; add further presets when a concrete use case demonstrates what differs.

Generated facts

Generated/ holds disposable source-derived notes. Each records its source and export revision. Regeneration should reconcile stable IDs, report removals, and detect broken mappings.

Your architectural exploration

Workspace/ holds your annotations, questions and proposed connections. Regeneration preserves it. Accepted architectural facts move through review into the appropriate canonical repo source.

01 · What the words mean

One focus. Several kinds of connection.

K-Plex means Knowledge Plex. Its README describes a spatial navigator inspired by TheBrain. Clicking a neighbor brings that note to the center. The arrangement stays meaningful as you move. K-Plex README.

A sibling shares a parent. It is derived from two parent-child links, rather than requiring a third manually maintained connection. A node can have several parents, so this is a graph with overlapping neighborhoods.

The phrase “left and right siblings” obscures a useful distinction: the sides can represent different relationships. TheBrain's documented normal Plex has jumps on the left and siblings on the right. TheBrain help.

In graph theory, a k-plex is a relaxed clique: each vertex in a set S has at least |S| - k neighbors within S. That density concept does not define this navigation layout. ListPlex research paper.

Schematic of documented roles, not a product screenshot. Position is a navigation convention; an edge still needs a specific meaning.

Three meanings that must stay separate

Hierarchy: parent ↔ child.
Sequence: previous ↔ next.
Association: friend ↔ friend.

K-Plex's current source treats challengers symmetrically too. Two roles can occupy one side without meaning the same thing. Relationship inverse rules (source inspection, not a runtime test).

Why a reference is not automatically a parent

A page can cite an ADR, use a term, or compare alternatives. None of those statements alone means “is a child of.”

K-Plex can infer different roles from ordinary links depending on settings. For ViViEfs, inferred mentions should stay visibly distinct from declared semantic relationships. Inference source.

03 · Start with what the repo already knows

The definition already has a home.

The docs already connect terms, ADRs, decisions, guides and claims. A focused graph could expose those connections together.

The unit should be a concept or a record, not always a file. “Datom” and “Changeset” share GLOSSARY.md, yet need different neighborhoods.

The existing parser already extracts terms and gives them anchors. K-Plex's documented section expansion follows headings; our bold glossary entries would need explicit extraction or mapping. Repo term parser; K-Plex sections.

Design source for this research page: the project's actual Starlight dark palette, typography and blue links, sampled from the running docs site.

04 · Try the idea on real terms

From “Datom” to where it matters.

Click a neighbor to recenter. Try Datom → Changeset → Commit datom, then return to the guide and compare its children. Each focus also offers a concrete code reference and rationale.

Hand-curated research prototype Layout follows TheBrain's parent / child / jump / sibling convention. Here, the hierarchy means teaching context, not domain containment. These are selected relationships, not an exhaustive graph. The same concept can appear in two regions when it has two different roles.

The gate link identifies the qualifying claim. This prototype does not read the current ledger and does not claim a fresh pass. The log-store guide is draft; the changesets teaching group represents a planned guide. A real view must show those distinctions.

What this earlier teaching sketch tests: can you explain why Datom and HLC are siblings here, why a datom's membership in a changeset is a different relationship, and where to inspect the actual code? If the picture makes those harder, its relationship model needs work.
05 · What would make it maintainable?

Store the meaning. Derive the picture.

The graph should be disposable. The definitions, declared relationships and evidence should survive any viewer.

01

One authoritative home

Read definitions from the glossary, teaching from guides, decisions from ADRs, and evidence from its existing records. Editing a graph label must not create a second definition.

02

Explain every connection

Keep subject, relationship, target and source location. Distinguish an explicit declaration, a mechanical derivation and a suggested inference. Clicking a connection should reveal why it exists.

03

Keep views small and purposeful

“Learn this term”, “Find its usage”, and “Inspect its evidence” can select different connections. Keep counts, a list view, history and deep links so hidden neighbors stay discoverable.

Connection to showWhere it can come fromHow much is known?
Term → definitionExisting glossary parser and anchorsExtractable today
Guide → ADR / gate / exemplarExisting guide frontmatter; project metadata.guidesDeclared today
Page → mentions termThe existing reference and term matching machineryDerivable mention; it does not establish semantic ownership.
Guide → teaches termToday: concepts prose and headings. Proposed: a small explicit mapping where ambiguous.Needs a schema decision
Term → related conceptSpecific glossary / guide statements, curated with source locationsA prose link alone is insufficient to infer its kind.
Term → used in symbolExplicit code-symbol mapping, then mechanically resolved locationsA name match alone is insufficient. The prototype uses inspected examples.
Sibling ↔ siblingShared parent under the same selected relationshipDerive at read time. Do not author sibling edges separately.
Claim → current evidence statusGate definitions and machine-written ledger / freshness rulesRead the authoritative result. Never infer “passed” from an ADR label.

Repo sources: references, term linking, guide frontmatter, project metadata, gates. Sources were inspected locally; repository links point to main for convenience.

Don't turn “builds on” into “contains”

The glossary explicitly says patterns do not nest. A workflow pattern building on the log store should get a labeled dependency connection, not become its child pattern. A teaching hierarchy is a separate view.

Canonical “Builds on” definition

Keep prose for explanations that need a sequence

A neighborhood helps answer “what is related?” A walkthrough still explains atomic changeset visibility or a workflow resuming after a crash. Use the graph to enter that explanation and return from it.

This is a design hypothesis about comprehension. We have not run a learner study or benchmarked either product with this repo.

06 · Routes worth considering

Explore first. Choose ownership deliberately.

A · Selected first experiment

K-Plex in a small vault

Gain: experience an existing spatial navigator and relationship editing.

Tradeoff: an export must bridge our term granularity, MDX and code references. Test those before assuming whole-repo compatibility.

Boundary: generated notes plus a separate human-owned exploration area. Proposed relationships can be reviewed before becoming canonical repo facts.

B · Possible later use

Curated views in teaching

Gain: canonical sources, shareable term URLs, existing rendering, version history and verification.

Tradeoff: we must define semantic edges, interactions, accessibility and extraction ourselves.

What remains unproven: whether a selected graph view improves a particular lesson. Lesson structure should decide the interaction, rather than inheriting open-ended browsing.

C · Separate workspace

TheBrain as a companion

Gain: an established dedicated environment for associative navigation.

Tradeoff: mapping, synchronization and source ownership become ongoing responsibilities.

Best fit: a personal thinking workspace when maintaining a separate Brain is itself desirable.

Recommendations above are research judgments. They do not change the repo's accepted design. K-Plex's AGPL licence is a separate question from studying its interaction model; no dependency adoption is proposed here.

A small evaluation that would answer the real question

Start with 15-25 concepts spanning Datom, Changeset and Workflow, plus a few guides, ADRs, code symbols and claims. Ask a newcomer to (1) explain one term, (2) contrast two related terms, and (3) find an actual usage and its evidence. Compare with the existing docs.

Then rename a term, move a source and change one declared relationship. Check that the graph either updates or reports the broken source, with no stale duplicate definition. Only expand if both comprehension and maintenance improve.
